translation: The element of space in the east and the south is endless. It is endless in the west and the north, too. It is above and below. It fills all the ten directions. Space is exactly the same everywhere. It has no differences at all.

academic_translation:
Whatever is the suchness of the past, the suchness of the future,
Whatever is the suchness of the present, the suchness of the arhats,
Whatever is the suchness of all phenomena, the suchness of the Victors—
All this suchness of phenomena is without distinction.
translation: There is the way things really are in the past and future. There is the way things really are right now. There is the way things really are for the worthy ones. There is the way things really are for all things and for the Victorious Ones. The way things really are has no differences at all.

The awakening of the Well-Gone Ones is free from separate things. An awakening hero might want to reach this. They must use clever ways and practice the perfection of wisdom. Without the wisdom of the Guides, they will not reach it.

academic_translation:
If a bird with a massive body of one hundred and fifty yojanas,
Whose wings are exhausted, lacks strength and skill,
And leaps from the abode of the Thirty-Three to this Jambudvīpa,
It will surely meet with ruin there.
translation: Imagine a huge bird that is one hundred and fifty leagues big. Its wings are tired. It has no strength or skill. If it jumps from the home of the Thirty-Three down to this Jambudvipa, it will surely crash and be ruined.

academic_translation:
Even if these five perfections of the Victors
Are accomplished for many tens of millions and hundreds of billions of eons,
And infinite, vast aspirations are constantly relied upon in the world,
Without skillful means and devoid of wisdom, one falls into the very state of a śrāvaka.
translation: You could practice the five perfections of the Victorious Ones for billions of ages. You could constantly make huge, endless wishes in the world. But if you lack clever ways and wisdom, you will just fall into the state of a listener.

academic_translation:
Whoever wishes to definitely emerge in this Buddha vehicle,
With an even mind toward all beings and the perception of them as parents,
Should strive with a beneficial attitude and a mind of loving-kindness,
And, being without harshness and straightforward, speak gentle words.
translation: Anyone who wants to truly ride in this Buddha's vehicle must have a fair mind toward all beings. You should see them as your parents. Try to help them with a mind of loving-kindness. Be honest, never be mean, and always speak gentle words.

academic_translation:
The elder Subhūti fully requested of the Protector of the World:
"Please teach the signs of those free from afflictions, an ocean of qualities,
And how those of great power will not turn back again;
Thus, may the Victor grant a prophecy of just a fraction of their qualities."
translation: The elder Subhuti asked the Protector of the World a question. He said, "Please teach me the signs of those who are free from mental trouble. They have an ocean of good qualities. How do these powerful people avoid turning back? May the Victorious One give a prediction about just a tiny part of their good qualities."

academic_translation:
Free from the perception of diversity, they speak words endowed with reason,
And do not rely on other śramaṇas and brahmins;
These wise ones have constantly abandoned the three lower realms at all times,
And they strive intensely on the path of the ten virtuous actions.

locked_terms.use: path of the ten good actions

translation: They are free from the idea of differences, and they speak sensible words. They do not rely on other holy wanderers or priests. These wise people always avoid the three lower realms. They work very hard on the path of the ten good actions, doing the ten good deeds.

academic_translation:
Without material motives, they teach the Dharma to beings,
Taking singular delight in the Dharma and always endowed with gentle words;
They are fully endowed with alertness while going, walking, sleeping, and sitting,
And they walk looking ahead only the length of a yoke, their minds free from delusion.
translation: They teach the teaching to beings without wanting any reward. They find great joy in the teaching. They always speak gentle words. They are staying alert while going, walking, sleeping, and sitting. They walk looking ahead only the length of a yoke. Their minds are free from confusion.

They make themselves clean and wear clean clothes. The three are kept quiet and pure. These great leaders do not want to gain things. They always want the teaching. They have passed beyond the world of Mara. They do not depend on anyone else. They practice the four kinds of deep focus, but they do not stay stuck in that deep focus.

academic_translation:
They do not desire fame, and their minds are not entangled by anger.
Even if they become householders, they are always unattached to all things.
For the sake of livelihood, they do not seek resources by terrible means.
They do not practice mantras for fierce actions, nor mantras for bringing women under one's control.
translation: They do not want fame. Their minds are not tangled in anger. Even if they live as a householder, they never cling to anything. To earn a living, they do not do terrible things. They do not use words of power to hurt others or to control women.

academic_translation:
They do not prophesy whether beings with the karma of desire will become male or female.
Utterly secluded, devoted to the perfection of wisdom, they are free from conflict and dispute, and their mind of loving-kindness is firm.
Desiring omniscience, they always possess a mind inclined toward the teachings.
translation: They do not predict if beings caught in desire will be born as boys or girls. They stay quiet and focus on perfect wisdom. They do not fight or argue. Their mind of loving-kindness is strong. Because they want the state of knowing everything, their minds always turn to the teachings.

academic_translation:
They completely abandon the borderlands of barbarian peoples.
Without doubt about their own stage, they are always like Mount Meru.
They sacrifice even their lives for the sake of the Dharma and strive intensely in yoga.
One should know that these are the signs of the irreversible.
translation: They stay completely away from any rough borderland. They have no doubts about their path. They always stand as firm as Mount Meru. They would even give up their lives for the teaching. They work very hard at their training. You should know these are the signs of never turning back.

academic_translation:
Form, feeling, perception, volition, and consciousness
Are profound, by nature signless, and utterly peaceful.
Just as one might search for the bottom of the ocean with an arrow,
When they are examined with wisdom, the depth of the aggregates is not found.
translation: Form, feeling, idea, intention, and awareness are very deep. By nature they are without signs and completely peaceful. Imagine trying to find the bottom of the ocean by shooting an arrow. In the same way, when you look with wisdom, you cannot find the bottom of these heaps.

academic_translation:
Any bodhisattva who has thus become profound,
And in the ultimate, unattached vehicle where the aggregates,
Elements, and sense bases do not exist, realizes this Dharma—
What perfectly accomplished merit is there beyond theirs?
translation: Think of an awakening hero who has become this deep. They ride in the highest, free vehicle. In the deepest truth, no heap, element, or sense door exists. When they understand this teaching, they perfect their stored-up goodness. What stored-up goodness could ever be greater than theirs?

academic_translation:
For example, a man who engages in the phenomena of desire,
Having made an appointment with a woman, failing to meet her—
However many conceptual thoughts his mind engages in for a single day,
The bodhisattva will obtain the merit accumulated over that many eons.
translation: Think of a man caught up in things of wanting. He plans to meet a woman, but they miss each other. Think of how many busy thoughts fill his mind in a single day. An awakening hero will gain goodness built up over exactly that many ages.

academic_translation:
Even if any bodhisattva, for many billions of eons,
Practices generosity toward arhats and pratyekabuddhas and maintains ethical discipline,
For whoever speaks the Dharma endowed with the supreme perfection of wisdom,
That generosity and ethical discipline do not match a fraction of the goodness of speaking it.
translation: An awakening hero might practice generosity toward worthy ones and solitary Buddhas. They might keep good conduct for billions of years. But imagine someone else who speaks the teaching of the supreme perfect wisdom. That generosity and good conduct do not even match a tiny part of the goodness of speaking this teaching.

academic_translation:
Any bodhisattva who meditates on supreme wisdom,
And arising from that, teaches the untainted Dharma,
And dedicates that for the sake of beings as a cause for awakening—
There is no virtue equal to that in the three worlds.
translation: An awakening hero might meditate on supreme wisdom. Then they get up and share the pure teaching. They dedicate this for the sake of all beings to help them reach awakening. In all the three worlds, there is no goodness equal to that.

academic_translation:
Knowing that merit, too, is hollow and likewise empty,
Insubstantial, baseless, and without essence,
If one thus engages in the wisdom practice of the Sugatas,
While engaging, one fully grasps immeasurable merit.
translation: You must know that stored-up goodness is hollow and empty. It has no solid base and is without a core. If you practice the wisdom of the Well-Gone Ones like this, you will gather stored-up goodness that cannot be measured.

academic_translation:
Spoken by the Buddha, extensively set forth and clearly taught,
Knowing all these Dharmas to be nothing but mere expressions,
Even if one were to speak of them for many tens of millions and hundreds of billions of eons,
In the dharmadhātu, there is no exhaustion and no increase.
translation: The Buddha has clearly and widely explained the teaching. But you must know that all of this teaching is just words. Someone might speak about it for billions of ages. Even so, the expanse of all things never runs out and never grows larger.

academic_translation:
Whatever is called the perfection of the Victors,
Those phenomena, too, are fully proclaimed to be mere names.
A bodhisattva who dedicates without conceit
Will not decline and will touch the supreme awakening of a Buddha.
translation: People talk about the perfection of the Victorious Ones. But even those things are said to be just a name. An awakening hero must dedicate their goodness without any self-importance. Then they will not fall back, and they will reach the highest awakening of a Buddha.

academic_translation:
Just as, by the first contact of the flame with the wick of an oil lamp,
The wick is not consumed, yet without it, it is not consumed,
And by the final contact with the flame, the wick is not consumed,
Yet without the final flame, the wick is not consumed.
translation: Think about an oil lamp. When a flame first touches the wick, that first touch does not burn up the wick. Yet without it, the wick would not burn. When the flame touches the wick for the last time, that last touch does not burn up the wick either. Yet without that last flame, the wick would not burn.

academic_translation:
By the first mind, supreme awakening is not touched,
Yet without it, one is not able to touch it.
By the final mind, peaceful awakening is not attained,
Yet without it, one is not able to attain it.
translation: The first thought does not touch highest awakening. But without that first thought, you cannot touch it. The final mind does not reach peaceful awakening. But without that final mind, you cannot reach it.

academic_translation:
From a seed, a sprout, a flower, and a fruit arise,
And when it ceases, it is not that the tree is absent—just as,
Likewise, the first mind is also the cause of awakening,
And when it ceases, it is not that awakening is absent.
translation: A seed grows into a sprout, then a flower, and then fruit. When the seed is gone, the tree is still there. In the same way, the first thought in your mind is the cause of awakening. When that first thought is gone, it does not mean awakening is gone.

academic_translation:
By drops of water, from the first to the last,
A vase is gradually, little by little, completely filled—just as,
Likewise, the first mind is also the cause of supreme awakening,
And by gradually perfecting virtuous qualities, one becomes a Buddha.
translation: Drop by drop, a vase slowly fills with water. In the same way, the first thought in your mind is the cause of the highest awakening. By slowly building up every good quality, you perfect the quality of goodness and become a Buddha.

academic_translation:
Practicing the phenomena of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness,
They do not touch nirvāṇa and do not engage in signs—
Just as a skilled boatman, though going back and forth,
Dwells on neither shore, nor does he dwell in the ocean.
translation: They practice the things of emptiness, being without signs, and without wishes. They do not touch peace beyond sorrow, and they do not follow signs. They are like a skilled boatman going back and forth. He does not stay on either shore, and he does not stay in the ocean.

academic_translation:
A bodhisattva practicing in this way has no conceit, thinking, "I
Will receive a prophecy from the ten powers and will touch awakening,"
Nor do they fear awakening, thinking, "There is nothing at all here";
To practice in this way is to practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
translation: An awakening hero who practices this way is not proud. They do not think, "I will get a prediction from the ten powers and I will touch awakening." They are also not afraid of awakening. They do not think, "There is nothing here at all." To practice this way is to practice the wisdom of the Well-Gone Ones.

academic_translation:
Seeing the wilderness paths of the world, along with famine and disease,
They are without fear and then put on their armor;
Always striving until the final limit of the future and fully understanding,
They do not generate even a speck of a weary mind.
translation: They see the wild paths of the world, along with hunger and sickness. They are not afraid, and they put on their armor. They always work hard until the very end of the future. They understand everything fully, and they never feel even a speck of a weary mind.
